Medical History

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Working Diagnosis and impressions: Fever with systemic symptoms after travel; ongoing febrile illness with malaise and myalgias; focal source not yet identified. Malaria is strongly considered given travel history; differential includes other travel-associated infections and occult sepsis.
- Relevant differential diagnoses and reasoning (aligned with transcript and consistent with DDx):
  - Malaria — High likelihood given recent rural Vietnam travel, fever with night sweats and myalgias; malaria testing planned (thick and thin films).
  - Leptospirosis — Medium likelihood given rural farmland exposure; compatible fever/myalgias; no classic signs required for consideration.
  - Enteric fever (typhoid) or similar travel-associated infection — Medium likelihood given travel history and fever; anorexia/nausea present; GI symptoms not prominent.
- Important notes on DDx vs transcript: No direct conflicts identified between transcript and DDx content.

Management Plan

- Immediate actions: Patient advised not to return to work until evaluated; arrange urgent blood testing and clinical assessment.
- Investigations planned: Malaria testing with thick and thin blood films; inflammatory markers; additional infectious workup as indicated.
- Referrals/appointments: Referral/booking to occur via clinic administration; option to attend a central London clinic or local A&E for prompt assessment; patient instructed to call the number in consultation notes after a short wait to be slotted in.
- Treatments: Symptom relief with OTC analgesics (patient has been using ibuprofen and paracetamol); no specific antimicrobial therapy started at this time pending test results.
- Patient education and precautions: Discussed need to identify source of fever; potential travel-related infections; advised on when to seek urgent care (worsening symptoms, confusion, chest pain, shortness of breath, persistent high fever, or inability to keep fluids down).
- Follow-up: To be guided by test results and specialty assessment; arrange result review and further management as needed.
- Considerations (DDx-supported reasoning for actions): If malaria or other infections confirmed, initiate appropriate treatment per results; if sepsis suspected, escalate accordingly.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Malaria
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Travel to rural Vietnam; fever with night sweats and myalgias; prophylaxis taken; malaria testing planned.
- Leptospirosis
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Rural farmland exposure; fever and myalgias; incubation window compatible.
- Enteric fever (typhoid) or travel-associated infection
  - Likelihood: Moderate
  - Justification: Travel history and fever with malaise; anorexia/nausea; incubation compatible; GI symptoms not prominent.
- (Note: Other DDx such as dengue or occult septicemia were considered in the broader differential but are lower probability given the current presentation; not listed here as top 2–3 per transcript/consensus.)
